title: All subsequences of a string - GeeksforGeeks
content:
Given a string, we have to find out all its subsequences of it. A String is said to be a subsequence of another String, if it can be obtained by deleting 0 or more character without changing its order.

For example, sub-sequences of "geeks" are

Examples: 

Input : ab
Output : "", "a", "b", "ab"

Input : abc
Output : "", "a", "b", "c", "ab", "ac", "bc", "abc"

Try It Yourself

Table of Content

  • Pick and Don't Pick Recursion - O(n × 2 ^ n) Time and O(n × 2 ^ n) Space
  • Incremental - O(n × 2 ^ n) Time and O(n × 2 ^ n) Space
  • Binary Representation - O(n × 2 ^ n) Time and O(n × 2 ^ n) Space

Pick and Don't Pick Recursion - O(n × 2 ^ n) Time and O(n × 2 ^ n) Space

We begin with the last character and for every character, we make two choices,

  • Pick: make a recursive call for next index and current subsequence appended with the current character.
  • Do Not Pick: make a recursive call for next index and current subsequence as it is.
C++ 
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

void solve(int i, string &s, string curr, vector<string>& ans) {
    if (i == s.length()) {
        ans.push_back(curr);
        return;
    }

    // Pick the current character
    solve(i + 1, s, curr + s[i], ans);

    // Don't pick the current character
    solve(i + 1, s, curr, ans);
}

vector<string> powerSet(string &s) {
    vector<string> ans;

    solve(0, s, "", ans);

    sort(ans.begin(), ans.end());
    return ans;
}

int main() {
    string s = "abc";

    vector<string> ans = powerSet(s);

    for (string str : ans)
        cout << str << " ";

    return 0;
}
Java 
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Collections;

class GFG {

    static void solve(int i, String s, String curr,
                      ArrayList<String> ans) {

        if (i == s.length()) {
            ans.add(curr);
            return;
        }

        // Pick the current character
        solve(i + 1, s, curr + s.charAt(i), ans);

        // Don't pick the current character
        solve(i + 1, s, curr, ans);
    }

    static ArrayList<String> powerSet(String s) {
        ArrayList<String> ans = new ArrayList<>();

        solve(0, s, "", ans);

        Collections.sort(ans);
        return ans;
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        String s = "abc";

        ArrayList<String> ans = powerSet(s);

        for (String str : ans)
            System.out.print(str + " ");
    }
}

Further Optimization : Instead of generating a substring every-time, we can pass index as additional parameter and pass reference of the same string.

Incremental - O(n × 2 ^ n) Time and O(n × 2 ^ n) Space

Start with an empty subsequence.

For each character,

  • Create new subsequences by adding the current character to every existing subsequence,
  • Then add these new subsequences to the result.
C++ 
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

vector<string> powerSet(string &s) {
    vector<string> ans = {""};

    for (char ch : s) {
        int size = ans.size();

        // Add current character to existing subsequences
        for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
            ans.push_back(ans[i] + ch);
        }
    }

    sort(ans.begin(), ans.end());
    return ans;
}

int main() {
    string s = "abc";

    vector<string> ans = powerSet(s);

    for (string str : ans)
        cout << str << " ";

    return 0;
}
Java 
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Collections;

class GFG {

    static ArrayList<String> powerSet(String s) {
        ArrayList<String> ans = new ArrayList<>();
        ans.add("");

        for (char ch : s.toCharArray()) {
            int size = ans.size();

            // Add current character to existing subsequences
            for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
                ans.add(ans.get(i) + ch);
            }
        }

        Collections.sort(ans);
        return ans;
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        String s = "abc";

        ArrayList<String> ans = powerSet(s);

        for (String str : ans)
            System.out.print(str + " ");
    }
}

Binary Representation - O(n × 2 ^ n) Time and O(n × 2 ^ n) Space

There are 2ⁿ possible subsequences, so consider every number from 0 to 2ⁿ - 1.

  • Treat each number as a bitmask
  • A set bit means the corresponding character is included in the subsequence and an unset bit means it is skipped.

For a string of length n, there are exactly 2ⁿ subsequences.

  • Generate numbers from 0 to 2ⁿ - 1.
  • Consider each number as a binary representation.
  • Each bit corresponds to one character.
  • Bit = 1 → include the character.
  • Bit = 0 → skip the character.

For "abc":

  • 000 → ""
  • 001 → "c"
  • 010 → "b"
  • 011 → "bc"
  • 100 → "a"
  • 101 → "ac"
  • 110 → "ab"
  • 111 → "abc"

Thus, every possible combination of characters is generated

C++ 
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

vector<string> powerSet(string &s) {
    int n = s.length();
    vector<string> ans;

    // Generate all possible bitmasks
    for (int mask = 0; mask < (1 << n); mask++) {
        string curr = "";

        // Check each bit
        for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
            if (mask & (1 << j))
                curr += s[j];
        }

        ans.push_back(curr);
    }

    sort(ans.begin(), ans.end());
    return ans;
}

int main() {
    string s = "abc";

    vector<string> ans = powerSet(s);

    for (string str : ans)
        cout << str << " ";

    return 0;
}

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Collections;

class GFG {

    static ArrayList<String> powerSet(String s) {
        int n = s.length();
        ArrayList<String> ans = new ArrayList<>();

        // Generate all possible bitmasks
        for (int mask = 0; mask < (1 << n); mask++) {
            String curr = "";

            // Check each bit
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                if ((mask & (1 << j)) != 0)
                    curr += s.charAt(j);
            }

            ans.add(curr);
        }

        Collections.sort(ans);
        return ans;
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {

        ArrayList<String> ans = powerSet(s);

        for (String str : ans)
            System.out.print(str + " ");
    }
}
